summary: For ages 6-7, build fluent (efficient, accurate, flexible) addition and subtraction within 10, moving children from counting toward recall and derived-fact reasoning (bonds to 10, doubles and near-doubles, +/−0 and +/−1). Anchor facts in strategies so a forgotten fact can be reconstructed, link each addition to its subtraction partner as fact families, and consolidate with short, frequent, interleaved retrieval. The primary proposal is adaptive strategy-anchored retrieval practice with fading visual support; a fixed quiz, a static strategy anchor, and oral quick-fire are preserved as complementary tools with different purposes.
misconceptions: Persisting with count-all/count-on for every fact instead of using derived facts or recall.
Mastering additions but not the related subtractions within 10.
Treating fluency as pure speed, leading to errors under pressure or anxiety.
Not recognising doubles/near-doubles as a shortcut (computing 6+7 from scratch).
Confusing similar facts (7+2 vs 7+3) when practice isn't interleaved.

activities.title: Adaptive fluency practice with fading ten-frame support
steps: Answer within-10 facts presented one after another (e.g. 6 + 4, 7 + 2, 9 − 4, 10 − 6), aiming to say the answer without counting.
Start with a faint ten-frame (or rekenrek image) behind each fact; as the child answers quickly, let the visual fade so they move from 'seeing' to recalling.
When a child stalls on a harder fact like 4 + 5, surface a strategy hint that shows the near-double (4 + 4 and one more) so they reconstruct rather than freeze.
Use a fact-family mode that surfaces the related subtraction for each bond (6 + 4 = 10 alongside 10 − 4 = 6, 10 − 6 = 4).
Interleave fact types (doubles, bonds, near-doubles, +/−1) so the child discriminates between similar facts (7 + 2 vs 7 + 3) rather than pattern-guesses.
activities.insight: A hard fact becomes easy when the child sees the double or bond inside it; isolated answers become a connected, flexible web of facts, including the subtraction partners — real fluency, not brittle speed.

activities.title: Interleaved fact quiz as a periodic check
steps: Work short sets of within-10 fact items (multiple-choice or fill-in-the-blank), kept low-stakes and quick.
Include related-subtraction pairs alongside additions (e.g. 6 + 4 and 10 − 6) so both are practised.
Interleave fact types within a set rather than grouping all doubles or all bonds together.
activities.insight: Quick retrieval across mixed facts shows which facts are recalled versus still counted, and keeps subtraction facts practised alongside their addition partners.

activities.title: Oral quick-fire warm-up
steps: Run a brief spoken quick-fire round of within-10 facts as a warm-up, e.g. '6 + 3? … 9 − 4? … 7 + 2? … 10 − 6?'

After an answer, ask follow-up questions: 'For 2 + 7, could you start from the 7 instead? Is it quicker?', 'How does knowing 6 + 4 = 10 help with 10 − 6?', 'Which did you just know without working out?', 'What's 9 − 4 — and how did you get it?'
activities.insight: Speaking facts aloud and explaining the strategy makes the child's recall-versus-counting visible and reinforces commutativity and fact-family links.

activities.title: Strategy reference anchor for derived facts
steps: Keep a visible reference wall or card of key derived facts and strategies: doubles (two equal rows), near-doubles (one extra), bonds to 10 on a ten-frame, and fact-family triangles linking a bond's + and − facts.
Point to the matching strategy when a fact is forgotten so the child reconstructs it (e.g. find 4 + 5 via 4 + 4 and one more).
activities.insight: Having the underlying strategies visible helps children recognise and reconstruct facts meaningfully instead of guessing.

checkQuestion: As fast as you can, no counting: 6 + 3? … 9 − 4? … 7 + 2? … 10 − 6?
checkAnswer: 9, 5, 9, 4 — from memory or instant derivation, including the bond-to-ten 10 − 6.
